> **The new billing dashboard is live.** It replaced the old Billing tab this morning. Nothing to install, nothing to migrate.
>
> What you get:
>
> - **Invoices and usage in one view.** Current-cycle usage refreshes hourly instead of settling at month close.
> - **Self-serve CSV export** per invoice, so no more filing a ticket for last quarter's numbers.
> - **Seat changes apply immediately** and show the prorated amount before you confirm it.
>
> It's at `Settings > Billing`. Old links redirect, so existing bookmarks and docs still land in the right place.
>
> Anything that looks wrong goes to `#billing-help`. If a number looks off, screenshot it before you refresh, the page rebuilds its state on load and the bad value is gone.

> **Code freeze runs the 20th through the 27th.** Last merge to `main` is 6pm on the 19th.
>
> While it's on:
>
> - **Sev1 and Sev2 fixes only.** Get an ack from the on-call lead in `#eng-oncall`, then merge.
> - **Keep reviewing everything else.** Open the PR, collect approvals, just don't merge. The queue drains on the 28th.
> - **Release branches stay open** for the fixes above, cut from `main` the usual way.
>
> If something has to land before the freeze, flag it today so we can size it. Work that shows up on the 19th is a no by default, and I'd rather say that now than at 5:45pm.

```
Fix duplicate charges on retried payments

A payment that timed out mid-capture generated a fresh idempotency key
on every retry, so the processor treated each attempt as a new charge.
Customers on a flaky connection could be billed two or three times for
one order.

Derive the idempotency key from the payment intent ID instead of the
attempt ID, so all retries of an intent collide on the same key. Treat
the processor's duplicate-key response as success rather than an error,
since it means the original capture already went through.

Existing double charges are not touched by this commit and still need
a refund sweep.

Fixes #4812
```

> **`GET /v1/transactions` is deprecated today and will be removed on [REMOVAL DATE, six months out].** After that date it returns `410 Gone` with no fallback.
>
> Until then the endpoint works exactly as it does now. No behavior changes, no rate-limit changes.
>
> **Move to `GET /v2/transactions`.** Three things differ:
>
> 1. **Pagination is cursor-based.** Replace `?page=2` with the `next_cursor` value from the previous response body.
> 2. **`amount` is an integer in minor units.** `12.50` becomes `1250`, and the currency is in the new `currency` field rather than implied by the account.
> 3. **`status` splits into `status` and `failure_reason`.** The old combined values like `failed_insufficient_funds` map to `status: "failed"` plus `failure_reason: "insufficient_funds"`.
>
> **Dates to put in your calendar:**
>
> - **[DEPRECATION DATE]:** responses start carrying `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers. Log them if you want an early warning that something still calls v1.
> - **[BROWNOUT DATE, one month out]:** first brownout, 1 hour of `410` responses so you find callers you forgot about. Second brownout runs [BROWNOUT DATE 2], 6 hours.
> - **[REMOVAL DATE]:** removed.
>
> Migration guide: [LINK]. If your integration can't move by the removal date, reply here before the first brownout so we know who's affected while there's still room to do something about it.

> **Subject:** Your workspace is ready
>
> Hi [FIRST NAME],
>
> Your [PRODUCT] workspace is live at [WORKSPACE URL]. You're the owner, so you can invite people and change anything in it.
>
> The fastest way to see whether this fits how your team works is to put one real project in it, not a test one:
>
> 1. **Create a project** and add the five or six tasks you're actually tracking this week.
> 2. **Invite two people** who work on those tasks. Sharing is what the tool is for, and it's dull alone.
> 3. **Set due dates** on anything with a real deadline, which turns on reminders and the timeline view.
>
> That takes about ten minutes and tells you more than a tour would.
>
> A few things worth knowing early: everything you do is undoable with `Cmd+Z`, including deletes. Your plan includes unlimited projects, so you don't need to be careful about creating one. And imports from Trello, Asana, and Jira are at [IMPORT URL] if you're moving existing work over.
>
> Reply to this email if you get stuck. It reaches a person on the product team, not a queue.
>
> [SENDER NAME]
> [PRODUCT]

> Hi [NAME],
>
> I can't refund the [DATE] charge. Our refund window is 30 days and this one is at [N] days, which puts it outside what I'm able to reverse.
>
> Here's what I can do:
>
> - **Cancel now so you're not billed again.** Your access stays active through [PERIOD END DATE] and nothing charges after that.
> - **Switch you to [CHEAPER PLAN]** at [PRICE]/month if the tool is still useful at a smaller size. The change applies at the next cycle.
>
> If the charge caught you by surprise because the renewal notice didn't reach you, tell me and I'll look at the send log. A notice that never arrived is a different problem than a missed deadline, and I'd treat it differently.
>
> Let me know which one you want and I'll take care of it today.
>
> [YOUR NAME]

One thing to settle before you send: I wrote this as a firm decline with alternatives, because that's the safe default. If your team can grant a one-time goodwill exception, swap the first paragraph for the exception and this becomes a much shorter email. That's a policy call, not a wording one, so it's yours.

> ## Day one
>
> The goal today is one merged PR, however small. Everything below exists to get you there. If you finish early, stop, day two has plenty.
>
> 1. **Check your accounts work.** You should have email, Slack, GitHub, and Okta from IT. Log into all four now. If any is missing, post in `#it-help` first thing, since access requests take a few hours and everything below depends on them.
> 2. **Get the repo running locally.** Clone `[ORG]/[MAIN REPO]`, then follow `docs/setup.md`. Budget an hour. Setup drifts, so when a step is wrong, fix the doc in the same PR you open at step 6.
> 3. **Run the test suite** with `make test`. A clean checkout should be green. If it isn't, that's a real bug, not you, so post the output in `#backend`.
> 4. **Point the app at the dev database.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and pull secrets with `[SECRETS COMMAND]`. Never point local at staging, writes there wake up on-call.
> 5. **Read three things**, in this order: `docs/architecture.md` for how services talk to each other, `docs/oncall.md` for what breaks and why, and the last month of `#incidents` for what actually broke.
> 6. **Open your first PR.** Pick anything from the `good-first-issue` label, or ship the setup-doc fix from step 2. Tag `[TEAM]` for review.
> 7. **Meet your onboarding buddy** for 30 minutes, [BUDDY NAME]. They booked time on your calendar. Bring the questions from steps 2 through 5, that's what the slot is for.
>
> **Who to ask:** `#backend` for code, `#it-help` for accounts and hardware, your manager for anything that feels like it shouldn't be your problem. Asking in a channel after 15 minutes stuck is the norm here, not a fallback.

> **File uploads failed for about 90 minutes today, from [START TIME] to [END TIME] UTC. Uploads work normally now.**
>
> **What you saw:** uploads stalled at 99% and then returned a generic error. Retrying didn't help while the incident was active. Everything else in the product, including files already stored, was unaffected.
>
> **What happened:** a configuration change to our storage layer rejected requests carrying the upload token our API issues. The change passed staging, where a different token format is in use, so we didn't catch it before it reached production. We rolled the change back and uploads recovered within minutes.
>
> **What it means for your data:** no files were lost or corrupted. Failed uploads never reached storage, so anything that errored has to be uploaded again. Files that reported success are intact and unchanged.
>
> **What we're changing:** staging now uses production token formats, so the same class of change fails there first. We're also adding an upload-success alert that pages within two minutes instead of waiting on customer reports, which is how we found this one.
>
> If you're still seeing upload errors, or you're missing a file you believe uploaded successfully, contact us at [SUPPORT EMAIL] with the file name and rough time. We'll trace it individually.

The timestamps, the token-format detail, and the two follow-up actions are placeholders shaped to be plausible. Replace them with what your timeline actually says before this goes out, since a customer-facing note that gets a detail wrong costs more than one that's late.

> This survey asks how it actually feels to build software here: your tools, your codebase, your on-call load, and whether the process helps or gets in the way. It takes about ten minutes and it's anonymous, with results reported only in groups of five or more so nothing traces back to you. Last year's version is why we funded the CI overhaul and killed the Thursday release meeting, so this is not a survey that goes into a drawer. Where something is bad, say it plainly. The comment boxes are the part we read most carefully. It closes [CLOSE DATE].

> ## [VERSION] — [DATE]
>
> ### Added
>
> - **Single sign-on (SAML 2.0).** Owners can connect an identity provider under `Settings > Security > SSO`. Okta, Entra ID, and Google Workspace are tested; any SAML 2.0 provider should work. Turning on **Require SSO** ends existing password sessions at the next page load, so plan for people to sign in again. SCIM provisioning is not in this release.
>
> ### Removed
>
> - **The legacy export button** is gone from the reports toolbar. It produced the old fixed-column CSV that no longer matched the report it came from. Use **Export > CSV**, which exports the columns you have on screen, including filters and sort order. The old endpoint `POST /reports/legacy-export` is also removed and returns `404`. If you were calling it from a script, switch to `POST /reports/export`, which takes the same report ID and returns the same file shape minus the three columns that were always empty.
>
> ### Fixed
>
> - Report filters no longer reset when you navigate back from a detail view.
> - Timezone on scheduled reports now follows the workspace setting instead of the server's.
>
> **Upgrading:** no migration steps. If you enable Require SSO, tell your team before you do it, since a forced sign-out with no warning generates a support ticket every time.

> **Subject:** [COMPANY] integration blocked 3 weeks, need an owner from your side
>
> Hi [ACCOUNT MANAGER NAME],
>
> Our integration with [VENDOR PRODUCT] has been blocked for three weeks and I need your help getting someone assigned to it. We're past the point where the support queue is going to resolve this.
>
> **Where it stands:** [BRIEF TECHNICAL BLOCKER, e.g. the webhook signature in your sandbox doesn't validate against the public key your docs publish, so we can't verify a single event]. Without it we can't move to production.
>
> **What's happened so far:**
>
> - **[DATE]:** opened ticket [TICKET NUMBER] with a reproducible case and request/response logs.
> - **[DATE]:** first response asked us to confirm details already in the ticket. We re-sent them the same day.
> - **[DATE]:** ticket moved to engineering. No update since, and two follow-ups from us went unanswered.
>
> **What we need:** a named engineer on your side and a call this week with them, our lead [NAME], and you. Thirty minutes with the right person is worth another month of ticket replies.
>
> Being direct about the impact: our launch date is [DATE] and this is the only item on the critical path. If we don't have a path forward by [DECISION DATE], we start evaluating [ALTERNATIVE], which neither of us wants after the work already spent here.
>
> Can you get us that call before [DAY]? I'll work around your team's schedule.
>
> [YOUR NAME]
> [TITLE], [COMPANY]
> [PHONE]

The dates, ticket numbers, and the specific blocker are placeholders written to read as real. Fill in your actual timeline before sending, and drop the alternative-vendor line if you're not willing to follow through on it, since an escalation that bluffs is worth less the second time.
